title: observability: token-level KV metrics, tracing, dashboards, and alert tuning
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: We need higher-fidelity visibility into token-level cost and latency and how KV cache behavior (hits/misses) affects end-to-end unit economics and tail latency. This PR adds new metrics, tracing spans, dashboards, and tuned alerts to help SREs and ML engineers detect regressions caused by KV cache degradation or rollout changes. Changes include: metric emission for per-request token_count, token_cost_estimate, kv_cache_hit_ratio; tracing span kv_cache.lookup with attributes (model, token_count, hit:boolean, ttl_ms); dashboards for token-level cost/latency breakdown and KV hit/miss heatmaps; alert tuning to reduce noisy paging while surfacing sustained regressions (examples below). Checklist: - [x] Emit new metrics (runtime) - [x] Add tracing spans and attributes - [x] Add Grafana dashboards and panels - [x] Add Prometheus alert rules + silences for known N-day noise - [x] Update docs and runbook - [x] Unit + integration tests. Impact: low-risk metric additions and dashboards; no behavior change to serving logic. Rollout plan: deploy metrics/tracing changes behind feature flag for 24h, validate dashboards in staging, then flip in prod. Related: ENG-2021 (observe KV regressions), SUP-3421 (customer report of token cost spike).

review_comments: Daniel Kim: Nice work. Two requests: 1) can we avoid emitting token_cost_estimate for very small requests (<3 tokens) to reduce cardinality? 2) add an example query for the dashboard README.
Ava Martinez: Reply: good call on cardinality. Added guard to skip token_cost_estimate if token_count < 3 and added example queries to docs. See commit e5f6a7b.
Priya Rao: Alert tuning looks sensible but the KV miss rate threshold seems aggressive for some heavy-TT models. Can we add model-scoped thresholds and a note in the runbook?
Ava Martinez: Reply: added model label to alert rules and included guidance in runbook about per-model baselines + how to override thresholds via /ops/alerts.
merge_summary: notes: Merged after approvals from Daniel Kim and Priya Rao. Feature flag enabled in staging; metric rollouts observed for 12h before enabling in prod.
release_notes: Observability: Added token-level KV cache metrics (redwood_runtime_kv_cache_hit_ratio) and token-level cost/latency metrics (redwood_runtime_token_cost_estimate, redwood_runtime_token_count)
Tracing: Added kv_cache.lookup span with hit/miss attributes for cross-service correlation
Dashboards: New Grafana dashboard 'Token + KV Overview' showing cost/latency breakdown and KV heatmaps
Alerts: Tuned Prometheus alerts for KV miss rate and token-cost regressions; per-model thresholds supported
notes_for_ops: Runbook: docs/observability/token_kv_metrics.md contains investigation steps and recommended queries
SLO impact: no direct SLO change; alerts intended to catch regressions before SLO violations
Rollout: metrics behind feature flag 'obs_token_kv_v1'; flip after 24h validation in staging
Known limitations: additional cardinality from per-model labels; we intentionally skip token_cost_estimate for requests with token_count < 3 to mitigate this
